reviewedProperties: Existing finite legacy source-interval API and fifteen prior tests remain valid.
New explicit bounded measurement start/end are distinct from original persistent runtime start; measurement completion invents no runtime end and performs no service control.
Current bounded original public account/inception/capital/run/source/start identity is required before any index request; observed identity and raw snapshot hash are retained.
Capture disconnection, stale snapshot and later recovery are sampled facts, never proof of continuous coverage; changed or stopped runtime closes enrollment for that binding.
A first validated actual runtime-end attestation remains latched even if its input file disappears.

Already-frozen independent active/control cohorts retain later indicative outcomes after a source change, separately from conservative runtime-comparable ranges and without runtime-performance credit.
Single physical index operation, maximum twenty-eight GETs, twelve-second pacing, response/evidence/resource bounds, no retries and prior provider cooldown/uncertainty accounting remain intact.
Only fixed keyless GeckoTerminal endpoints are requested; no Solana RPC, signing, ledger, financial writer, runtime controls or reporting architecture introduced.
limitations: Offline mocked verification does not establish provider availability, measured live sampler overhead, executable opportunities, profitability or whole-market recall.
Root must select the actual current source/run/public snapshot and settled prior provider receipt before starting collection; no live collection was started by this reviewer.
Public runtime observations are sampled and do not certify uninterrupted market capture between snapshots.
